faq_heading: New construction in Chilliwack: your questions answered

faq.q: What counts as new construction on this page?
faq.a: Active MLS® listings in Chilliwack where the board's age field is 0 or less: homes finished this year and homes listed before completion, in houses, townhomes and condos.

faq.q: Where are the newest homes in Chilliwack?
faq.a: Over the past year the newest sold homes were townhomes in Lower Landing: median build year 2025, 6 sales, median price $613,950.

faq.q: How fast do newer homes sell in Chilliwack?
faq.a: The quickest group among the newer ones was houses in Chilliwack Mountain: 15 days to sell at a median, closing at 97.1% of the list price.

blocks.text: The listings above are the active MLS® new-construction listings in Chilliwack, picked by setting the board's age field to 0 or less: homes completed this year and homes listed before they are finished. Land and income properties are excluded; houses, townhomes and condos are in. The search also includes Sardis, which has its own page with its own sold figures. Developers sell most presale homes themselves and list them on the MLS® late, if at all. Treat the search as the MLS® slice of new construction.
What newer homes in Chilliwack have sold for
In November 2025 to October 2026, townhomes in Lower Landing had the newest stock of any Chilliwack sub-area with enough sales to measure: median build year 2025, 6 sales, median price $613,950.
2 of 18 sub-area and home-type groups with 5 or more sales had a median build year of 2020 or later. The newest were Lower Landing townhomes (built 2025) and Lower Landing houses (built 2025).

items.t: Across Chilliwack, 294 houses sold at a median of $825,000, with the middle half between $695,938 and $1,038,038. They took 26 days and closed at 97.2% of the list price, and the median build year was 1980. The typical house sat on a lot of about 7,274 square feet. The median moved from $896,500 (November to January) to $749,950 (August to October).

Chilliwack townhomes over the past year: 108 sales, a median of $572,500, and a middle half from $437,025 to $642,750. The median home was built in 2004, took 29 days to sell and closed at 97.3% of list. Strata fees were a median $387 a month. The median moved from $578,950 (November to January) to $541,125 (August to October).

Across Chilliwack, 133 condos sold at a median of $310,000, with the middle half between $260,000 and $392,400. They took 36 days and closed at 96.7% of the list price, and the median build year was 1995. Strata fees were a median $397 a month. The median moved from $304,000 (November to January) to $290,000 (August to October).

Chilliwack duplexes over the past year: 9 sales, a median of $764,000, and a middle half from $605,000 to $840,000. The median home was built in 2003, took 73 days to sell and closed at 98.4% of list.

blocks.text: Planning and zoning notes for Chilliwack

items.t: Chilliwack's small-scale multi-unit housing amendment is Zoning Bylaw Amendment Bylaw 2024, No. 5395. It had first, second and third reading on June 4, 2024. The City says it allows up to four units on single-detached or duplex lots over 280 m² inside the urban growth boundary, and keeps two parking spaces per unit.
